title: For Spark's own savings products the flow rate limits are replaced by a supply cap and a maximum yield
content:
Each Spark Savings v2 instance states plainly that the usual controls do not apply: "The specific `maxAmount` and `slope` for this conduit's inflow/outflow are not defined for this Instance" (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.1.9.1.2.4, .9.2.2.4, .9.3.2.4). In their place sits a `Risk Parameters Current Configuration` block: ETH with "Supply cap: 500,000 WETH, Max yield: 5%, Current yield (at launch): 0%" (.9.1.4.2.1), USDC with a 2,000,000,000 cap at 10% (.9.2.4.2.1), USDT with 4,000,000,000 at 10% (.9.3.4.2.1).

The substitution follows from the direction reversal. A rate limit throttles an action Spark initiates; user deposits are initiated by strangers, and there is nothing for Spark to throttle at the moment of arrival. The meaningful controls become how much of the product may exist at all, and what it costs to fund.

So the risk vocabulary changes from velocity to capacity and price. A supply cap bounds the liability Spark can accumulate — the amount it must eventually redeem — while the yield ceiling bounds the cost of carrying it. Neither has an analogue in the inflow/outflow schema, and neither is expressible as a slope.

The caps also encode a view about where deposits can be productively deployed: 4bn USDT against 2bn USDC against 500,000 WETH, and a 5% yield ceiling on ETH against 10% on the dollar products. The savings side is sized by what the Liquidity Layer can profitably absorb, which is what makes the two halves of this registry a single system rather than two lists.
description: Savings instances state that inflow/outflow maxAmount and slope are not defined and instead publish risk parameters — 500,000 WETH cap at 5% max yield, 2bn USDC and 4bn USDT at 10%.
